request.spec:
A button downloads the period figures as a CSV file: a header line person,period,figure,carried
then one line per person and period, people in list order and periods in the order added, with the
figures as the rows show them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the period figures as a CSV file: a header line person,period,figure,carried
then one line per person and period, people in list order and periods in the order added, with the
figures as the rows show them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The new "Export periods (CSV)" button works: all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass, including the period-export test.

It's a single front-end change in `src/main/frontend/features/export/export.slot.tsx`, with no server, stored-data or audit changes. The file has the header `person,period,figure,carried`, then one line per person and period. People are in list order and periods in the order they were added. The figures are the same due-total and carried amounts the person rows show, formatted the same way.

The new test only checks files where every figure is `0.00`, so the export of non-zero figures hasn't been tested. It uses the same calculation the rows use, though, so it should match them.

Unlike the other exports, this one writes the figures currently on screen rather than re-reading them from the server first. If the screen hasn't yet caught up with a recent change, the file won't include it either.
